metadata.case_name: WONG HIN PUI v. MOK YING KIT AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: serious injury to his head; intracranial haematomas
source: He had sustained a serious injury to his head which ought to have been apparent to those at the Tai Po clinic who had kept him waiting and then sent him home.
He had two operations carried out on his head including evacuation of haematomas which had built up within his skull.
He developed a left-side hemiplaegia and epileptiform attacks requiring anti-convulsant treatment.

injuries.description: epileptiform attacks / seizure disorder requiring anti-convulsant treatment
source: He developed a left-side hemiplaegia and epileptiform attacks requiring anti-convulsant treatment.
He is currently taking Tegretol, Phenytoin and Epilim for this condition.
injuries.icd_description: Epilepsy due to injuries to the head

injuries.description: significant cosmetic defect (residual from skull surgery)
source: About one year after his discharge from convalescent hospital a cranioplasty was carried out.
He is nonetheless left with a significant cosmetic defect of which he tries to make light as much as he can, because he is such a patently decent, likeable, honest and philosophical man.
There is also a significant cognitive deficit as attested to by Professor Peter Lee and I do not need to detail this.

manifestations.description: left-sided hemiparesis affects his arms particularly severely; when the left hand grips, he needs to lever it open to release that grip; it has no capacity for fine movements
regular epileptiform seizures or convulsions which are focal in nature; sometimes he gets warning but not always; their incidence has diminished over the past two years
unable to respond to any verbal contact for a further week (post-accident acute state)
post-concussional disorder / post-concussional syndrome and depressive disorder / dysthymic disorders (psychiatric diagnoses given by experts)
considered unemployable on the open market by Dr Choa 'On the basis of his physical and neurological deficits, Dr Choa considers him to be unemployable on the open market.'

treatments_received.treatment: Two operations on his head including evacuation of haematomas
source: He had two operations carried out on his head including evacuation of haematomas which had built up within his skull.

treatments_received.treatment: Cranioplasty (about one year after discharge from convalescent hospital)
source: About one year after his discharge from convalescent hospital a cranioplasty was carried out.
He was in intensive care for 7 days.

treatments_received.treatment: Anti-convulsant medication: Tegretol, Phenytoin and Epilim
source: He is currently taking Tegretol, Phenytoin and Epilim for this condition.

treatments_future.treatment: Psychiatric/psychotherapeutic treatment (supportive psychotherapy twice a month for two years with a safety net of two to four sessions a year)
source: In Professor Lee's view the Plaintiff needed a degree of treatment but not intensively. He also needed monitoring. He needed supportive psychotherapy working on his residual capacity, probably for two years, twice a month with provision for a safety net of two to four sessions a year.

B. Neurological

This is agreed at $324,000.
As he will have an exercise machine, I think monitoring of his use of such a machine is the sensible and practical approach. The sum allowed will therefore be $86,400.
With domestic assistance the need will be initial only and he will have resource to other services. I will allow the figure put forward by the Defendants of $43,200.
The Defendants agree the sum of $388,800.

losses.description: He is nonetheless left with a significant cosmetic defect of which he tries to make light as much as he can.
Left-sided hemiparesis and reduced function of left hand; 'He developed a left-side hemiplaegia ...' and loss of fine movement in left hand limiting function.
He will need a domestic helper 'The domestic helper will be more or less full-time.' A round figure of $1,000,000 is allowed for future domestic services.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Need for domestic assistance and handyman services; handyman allowance $18,000.
Significant cognitive deficit as attested by Professor Peter Lee.
Loss of wife and child, loss of home and rejection by family as direct consequences of the injuries: 'These are all a direct consequence of the injuries he has suffered.'
He is considered unemployable on the open market and future loss of earnings awarded: monthly loss $21,294; future loss $4,088,448.
He will need to take taxis more often: allowance $200 per week over 10 years totalling $104,000.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Provision for exercise equipment: cost of two machines $106,000 (noted in Addendum) and total aids/equipment $28,512.
